visual.general_description: Two grayscale abdominal radiographs of an infant labeled A and B.
visual.detailed_description: Figure 1 is a two-panel composite of grayscale radiographs side by side, each with a bold white panel letter at the upper left. Panel A shows a frontal infant chest and abdomen with an enlarged, hazy abdomen, a gas-containing structure crossed by thin tube-like lines and small gas-filled loops. Panel B is a tilted, closer view of the upper abdomen with large dark gas-density zones beneath the ribs, a large central soft-tissue area and clustered loops in the lower middle. No text other than the panel letters is visible.

panels.general_description: Frontal grayscale abdominal and lower chest radiograph of an infant.
panels.detailed_description: Panel A is a frontal grayscale radiograph of an infant chest and abdomen with a bold white letter A at the upper left. The ribs and spine are visible and the lungs appear as darker fields above. The abdomen is large and rounded with a hazy, diffusely gray mid and upper abdomen. At the right of the image a rounded gas-containing structure is crossed by thin linear tube-like lines, and several small gas-filled loops sit in the lower left of the abdomen. The image has a faint grid or screen pattern, as if photographed from a display. No text other than the panel letter is visible.

imaging_modalities.visual_cue: Grayscale frontal radiograph showing ribs, spine and abdominal gas pattern
